en: One fascicle of the Essential Gate of the Spiritual Efficacy of the Dharani of Great Fulfillment and the Methods of Supernatural Arts Spoken by Vajra Ucchuṣma;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Ajita from the Kingdom of Northern India.
*Dāxiàn* (達霰) means "Invincible" (*anabhibhū*) in the language of Tang; it is translated as "Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Buddha was staying in the country of Kuśinagara, at the birthplace of the Mallas, between a pair of *śāla* trees on the banks of the Hiranyavatī River.
At that time, as the Tathāgata was about to enter parinirvāṇa,
there were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of beings— including devas, nāgas, the eight classes of supernatural beings, humans, and non-humans—
who stood on all four sides of the Buddha, weeping, sobbing, and remaining in a state of grief and distress.
At that time, there were also great assemblies of devas, including Śakra Devānām-Indra and others,
all of whom came to make offerings;
however, only the Brahma King Śikhin did not come.
The various celestial maidens sat surrounding him on all four sides;
in front and behind were thousands of myriads of koṭis of celestial maidens.
They were enjoying themselves together when they heard that the Tathāgata had entered parinirvāṇa, yet they did not come to pay their respects.
At that time, the great assembly spoke to them, saying:
"Today the Tathāgata is about to enter parinirvāṇa.
Why has that Brahmā King not come?
That king must surely possess a mind of conceit."
Yet he does not come here.
We shall dispatch our retinue of minor vidyādharas to go there and bring him back."
Having spoken these words, he exhorted hundreds of thousands of mantra-adepts and rishis,
and they arrived at that place;
there they saw all manner of impurities serving as its ramparts and moats.
When those seers saw this,
they each violated their vows and died.
At that time, the great assembly marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence.
Furthermore, he commanded immeasurable vajra-holders to escort the mantra-practitioner on his way;
for seven days, no one was able to capture him.
When the great assembly saw this, their sorrow redoubled.
At that time, the assembly spoke these verses with one voice:
"Alas, Great Holy One! Having entered the Truth, why so very soon?"
The devas remain resolute; alas, the devas call out after the Devātideva who has entered the truth like a fire being extinguished!
After the great assembly had spoken this verse, [the Buddha passed away].
They were doubly choked with emotion, weeping and wailing in grief.
At that time, the Tathāgata, out of compassion for the great assembly,
immediately employed his power of great universal knowledge.
From his left heart, he emanated the Invincible Vajra (*Abhedyavajra*).
Thereupon, rising from his seat in the midst of the assembly,
he addressed the great multitude, saying:
"I possess a great divine mantra capable of seizing that Brahmā King.
Having spoken these words, he immediately manifested great supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*) in the midst of the great assembly,
causing this trichiliocosm to shake in six ways.
The palaces of the devas, the palaces of the nāgas, and the palaces of all the spirits and ghosts were utterly shattered and collapsed.
He then immediately leaped up into the air and went to where the Brahmā King was,
pointing at him with his finger.
Those foul and impure substances were transformed into the great earth.
At that time, Vajra went to him and said,
"O Greatly Deluded One, I, the Tathāgata, am about to enter nirvāṇa."
"Why do you not go?
He then used the indestructible power of the vajra to lightly touch him with his finger.
The Brahma King resolved his mind and proceeded to the place where the Tathāgata was.
At that time, the great assembly praised him, saying:
"O Great Malla, you are indeed capable of such supernormal power."
He brought that Brahmā King here.
At that time, Vajra replied:
"If there are sentient beings in the world..."
Those who are troubled and disturbed by various devas, evil māras, and all heterodox practitioners need only recite my mantra one hundred thousand times;
I shall manifest my own form and cause all sentient beings to be fulfilled according to their wishes.
May they forever be free from poverty and always abide in peace and happiness.
The mantra is as follows.
First, one should make this great vow.
Homage to my original teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha.
After the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, I shall uphold this dhāraṇī and vow to deliver all sentient beings.
"May the Buddha-dharma not perish but abide long in the world.
Having spoken this vow,
he then recited the Great Perfection Dharani-mantra, the Vimalapada (Ugly Trace) True Word, as follows:

Oṃ hūṃ traḥ vaṃ mahā-praṇava-ghoṣa-vijaya-mānase oṃ svāhā. When the Vajra-holder had spoken this mantra, he said: "Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. At that time, having uttered this mantra, the Vajra-holder [spoke].
He further spoke these words:
"After the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, I shall constantly recite this mantra.
If there are sentient beings who request and vow to uphold this mantra,"
I have always served as a messenger for others, fulfilling their requests according to their wishes.
I now recite this divine mantra before the Tathāgata;
I only pray that the Tathāgata may, within the truth, clearly perceive us.
World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who are greatly afflicted and disturbed by various evil spirits and ghosts,
this mantra will be unable to cause them any harm.
They shall be forever free from suffering and calamity.
World-Honored One, if there are sons or daughters of good family who wish to cure the myriad illnesses, [they should recite this mantra].
Recite the above mantra four hundred thousand times.
When treating those who are ill, it will prove efficacious.
Whether they are pure or impure, you may employ them as you wish.
I shall follow and fulfill all your wishes.
If you wish to cause withered trees to sprout branches and leaves,
take one large *liang* of white resin incense (*guggulu*).
Anoint the heart of the tree with [the substance].
Recite the mantra over willow branches one hundred times.
If this is performed three times a day for three full days, flowers and fruit will immediately grow.
If one wishes to cause water to emerge from a dried-up spring,
one should encircle it with pure ash.
Then, take three *dou* of well-water and place it within the spring water.
If one recites the mantra one hundred and eight times during the third watch (the hour of the tiger),
water will surge forth like a chariot wheel.
If one wishes to cause withered mountains to grow grasses and trees, [one should perform this rite].
Take a blade of tempered steel and surround it within a mountain on all four sides;
recite the mantra three thousand times, and when seven days have passed, it will come to life.
If one wishes to cause wild beasts to submit and return,
one should take agallochum incense and burn it while facing the dwelling place of the beasts, reciting the mantra one thousand times.
Those beasts will arrive during the night.
They shall assemble at the doorways of those who uphold the Dharma;
like domestic animals among humans, they will submit to them,
being driven at will and never again forsaking them.
If you wish to cause the yakṣas to come of their own accord and submit,
take ten peach twigs and cut them into equal lengths.
Take one shi of water and boil it down until five dou remain.
Take peach and willow branches from a flood-stricken area.
Combine three taels of cloves, three taels of *stana-gandha* (nipple-incense), and three taels of *śrīveṣṭaka* (white resin incense).
Afterwards, mix these with willow water and boil until five *dou* remain.
Immediately place it in a broken basin.
Take a peach branch three feet long and stir the water while reciting the mantra one hundred times.
All the yakṣas and rākṣasas came forth to appear;
they spoke with those who practice the Dharma together,
requesting to become his attendants first.
If one wishes to extinguish the poisons of various evil spirits, ghosts, venomous snakes, scorpions, wild beasts, and the like,
one should take pure ashes and encircle the holes where they dwell;
then they will all emerge of their own accord.
When one recites this mantra in a low voice one hundred times,
all those such as snakes and other venomous creatures will each extinguish their poisonous intent and dare not harm humans.
One will swiftly attain liberation.
If one wishes to prevent a vicious dog from harming a person,
take a morsel of food, recite the mantra over it seven times, and give it to the dog to eat.
It shall never harm others nor emit sound.
If one wishes to cause an evil person to come and submit,
one should write that person’s name and place it beneath the feet of the practitioner reciting the mantra.
Recite this mantra one hundred times;
if you focus your mind on that person, they will arrive immediately,
subduing themselves and abandoning all thoughts of enmity and hatred.
If one wishes for two people to hate each other,
one should write down the names of those two individuals and recite the mantra over them two hundred and eighteen times beneath one's own feet.
Those people will then turn away from one another and no longer love or respect each other.
If there are those who harbor mutual hatred, and one wishes to cause them to love and respect one another,
one should immediately write down their names and surnames.
If one recites this mantra one hundred and eight times beneath one's own feet,
that person will come to hold one in deep affection and respect, never wishing to be parted from one.
Furthermore, it shall bring peace and happiness to those who are currently suffering and lack well-being.
Write the name of the person in question beneath [the mantra].
Recite the mantra three hundred times,
and for that person’s sake, you should make a great vow.
At that time, I personally delivered it myself;
with unimpeded eloquence, I followed the intentions of those who followed me and bestowed all that was required upon them.
If a mantra-practitioner seeks various precious treasures, such as *maṇi* jewels or wish-fulfilling gems (*cintāmaṇi*),
they need only recite the mantra with a sincere mind, setting their own limit for the number of recitations;
I shall then personally deliver [the treasures] to fulfill their wishes.
If one wishes to treat the illnesses of others,
one should form the mudrā for sudden illness;
first, with the left hand, use the index and middle fingers.
The *Yashuo* (Sealing) Text:
Recite the seal-mantra one hundred times and strike the patient seven times with the seal; they will be cured immediately.
If the patient is on the verge of death...
First, one should seal the five paths and then perform the treatment.
This is the Eye of the Seal of Immortality (*amṛtamudrā*).
Thus, first conforming to the seal, bend the ring finger toward the palm.
If one recites the mantra while holding up the little finger one hundred times, the affliction will be swiftly removed.
If treating those with demonic illnesses,
one need only do so at the side of the patient's head.
If one burns agalloch incense while reciting this mantra,
it will be immediately eliminated. This applies even to those afflicted by diseases caused by insects or poisons.
If one writes the name of the afflicted person on paper and recites the mantra over it, they will immediately recover.
To treat those with diseases caused by *jingmei* (malevolent spirits), one proceeds according to the same method.
If treating those with *fujian* disease, [one proceeds as follows].
Write down the name of the afflicted person and the name of the demon causing the illness;
bury it beneath the patient’s bed and recite the mantra over it.
That demon will then respectfully acknowledge the names and manifest its own form.
He then commanded that ghost to observe the events of the three periods of time;
as each matter was recounted in detail to the person, their illness was quickly cured.
This applies to anyone suffering from the disease of *shiqi* (epidemic pneuma).
When the mantra-practitioner sees this, the illness will immediately be cured.
If one wishes to prevent the King of Ghosts who spreads disease from entering a boundary,
one should recite this mantra of mine one thousand and eight times on the ten days of the *zhāi* (fasting) observances.
A Single Volume on the Essential Methods for the Miraculous Arts of the Great Fulfillment Dhāraṇī Spoken by Vajra Ucchuṣma, Capable of Eliminating Illnesses and Ailments from Ten Thousand Li.
